text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- New foreign minister Ismail Cem has made his priority the routing of the main pipeline for Azeri oil through Turkey.
- The financial foundations for the eigh-year education reform have been completed.
- The government has won a great victory with the passage of an eight-year compulsory education bill through parliament at the end of a marathon debate.
- Businessmen in the troubled southeast of Turkey say banks will not give them credit for investments.
- Twelve government MPs voted against the administration's education bill.
- The extra funding for the government's education reforms will largely come from levies on cigarettes and alcohol.
- The education ministry needs to find 8,100 new teachers and 12,000 new classrooms before September in order to implement the new eight-year education law.
- Conservative opposition leader, Tansu Ciller said she would not be forming an alliance with the Islamists in the next general election.
- Foreign minister Cem said Turkey's long-term aim is to join the European Union.
- Islamist leader Necmettin Erbakan is to apply to the consitutional court for the cancellation of the new education law.
